intent_en: To explain the relationship between the length of a day and a year on Mercury.
previous_intent: To explain how the unique relationship between the length of a Mercury year and a Mercury day leads to extreme temperature fluctuations on the planet.
narration_support: A Mercury year is shorter than a Mercury day
chart_support: A diagram showing Mercury and the Sun with arcs labeled with two durations, illustrating the rotation and orbital periods.
evidence_note: The narration mentions the relationship between day and year length (specifically that a year is shorter than a solar day), while the chart visualizes the rotation period (59 days) and orbital period (88 days). The chart supports the comparison of these time periods, though the specific values (59 vs 88) show the sidereal day is shorter than the year, whereas the narration likely refers to the solar day (176 days) being longer than the year (88 days).
